sections.h2: How does selling a house in Peachtree City, GA work?
sections.html:
A Peachtree City house sells with extras that few other Georgia markets have: a village identity, a link to the city's path network and often a registered golf cart. Owners generally compare a standard listing, a private sale and a cash offer. Census estimates put the population at 40,880 for mid-2025, up 6.9% from 38,241 in the 2020 base.

Survey data for 2020 to 2024 describe a city of owners. Homeowners occupy 72.1% of housing units, the median owner-occupied value is $482,500 and median household income reaches $113,987. Renting costs a median $2,086 a month, so some buyers price the two options against each other. Residents 65 and older make up 21.0% of the population, and 61.6% of adults hold at least a bachelor's degree.

sections.h2: How was Peachtree City laid out, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Developers assembled more than 12,000 acres of Fayette County in the 1950s, and Peachtree City received its charter on March 9, 1959. The plan divided the city into villages, each with its own shopping, recreation and elementary school. The current villages are Aberdeen, Braelinn, Glenloch, Kedron and Wilksmoor. The first plan imagined 80,000 to 110,000 residents. A 1985 revision cut the build-out goal to about 45,000.

The city sits in the Piedmont between 740 and 961 feet above sea level. Its lakes are Lake Peachtree at about 270 acres, Lake Kedron at about 240 and Lake McIntosh at about 650. In a listing, name the village and the nearest path link, because both shape how buyers picture daily life. McIntosh High School honors the Creek chief whose 1821 land cession helped create Fayette County.

sections.h2: How do golf cart paths and cart registration affect a sale?
sections.html:
The city counts more than 100 miles of shared-use paths and about 11,000 registered carts. A seller with a cart has paperwork to finish, and a buyer shopping for one should know the rules on the city's cart page:

  • New cart registrations are completed in person at City Hall, and owners must be 18 or older.
  • A cart must be registered within 10 days of purchase.
  • A seller must report the sale or removal of decals within 10 days using the Cart Release Form.
  • A move requires a change of address notice within 60 days.
  • Decals go on both the front and rear of the cart.
  • Low-speed vehicles may use the paths if limited to 20 mph, insured, tagged through the Fayette County Tag Office, driven by a licensed driver and fitted with an amber strobe light.

Residents pay $45 for a three-year renewal covering 2026 through 2028. A buyer who lives outside the city and pays no Peachtree City property tax owes a yearly path user fee on top of registration:

Peachtree City motorized cart charges

Decal$15 per year
Ownership transfer$15
Path user fee for owners outside the city$235 per year
Registration plus path fee, outside owners$250 per year

Source: City of Peachtree City, Paths and Motorized Carts page.

sections.h2: Can a buyer run a short-term rental from a Peachtree City house?
sections.html:
Only with a city permit. Stays of 30 consecutive days or less count as short-term, and since January 1, 2025 every such rental needs a permit, with a citywide cap of 135. Operators who could prove rentals and tax payments before the ordinance passed on November 7, 2024 went first. If they already exceed 135, all keep permits and no new ones issue until the count drops below the cap.

Rentals are allowed in residential zoning districts, but detached structures, guest houses, recreational vehicles and trailers cannot be rented this way. A permit lasts 730 days. Applicants provide:

  • The completed application and a guest occupancy agreement under O.C.G.A. 43-21-3.2
  • A copy of the deed showing the applicant owns the property
  • A notarized criminal background check consent and a notarized tax payment and ordinance affidavit
  • Homeowner association approval, if one applies

The Building Department and Fire Marshal also inspect the property. Fines rise with repeat violations, up to $500 for a first, $750 for a second and $1,000 for a third in 12 months, and the third also brings a 24-month revocation. If you market the house as an income property, ask city staff whether the permit follows the owner or the address before you tell a buyer it transfers.

sections.h2: How are Peachtree City property taxes assessed and appealed?
sections.html:
Fayette's Assessors' Office values real and personal property and takes homestead applications, while the Tax Commissioner bills and collects at 770-461-3652. For 2026, residential and commercial notices were mailed June 23, and the appeal deadline of July 7, 2026 has passed. Each year's notice opens a new 45-day appeal window, and the written appeal must be signed, dated and received inside it.

One Fayette change helps buyers: homestead applications are no longer cut off on April 1. If you owned and occupied the home on January 1, you can apply up to the end of that year's appeal window. Someone who moved in later applies after the next January 1. A recently purchased home needs a recorded warranty deed or settlement statement along with a Georgia driver's license showing the address.

Fayette's exemption page lists several tiers that a seller can point buyers toward:

  • The basic L1 homestead exemption reduces state and school M&O assessed value by $2,000 and county and fire M&O by $5,000.
  • The L7 floating exemption limits yearly growth of the school portion of a homesteaded value to the lesser of 3% or inflation, plus improvements.
  • Owners 62 by January 1 may qualify for a school tax reduction that rises from $2,000 to $4,000, and owners 65 may qualify for a 50% school tax reduction.
  • A 100% disabled veteran may qualify for an exemption of $126,526.

Call the Fayette Assessors at 770-305-5376 for the codes on your bill.

sections.h2: What does Georgia charge to transfer a Peachtree City house?
sections.html:
Before a deed is recorded, the clerk of superior court collects Georgia's transfer tax and stamps proof of payment on the document. The seller is liable, though many contracts push it to the buyer. Filing questions about the electronic PT-61 go to the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority at (800) 304-5174.

Ask the Fayette County clerk for the current recording fee list, and review the tax lines on the settlement statement before you sign.

sections.h2: Which route suits a Peachtree City house: listing, private sale or cash?
sections.html: A house in good shape near the paths and lakes has the best odds on the open market, at the cost of prep work, showings and repair talks. A private sale saves the commission. A cash buyer suits a deadline, an inherited house or a property too worn for lender financing, with a price that reflects the buyer's repair and resale costs. Get terms in writing, and settle with your attorney how the cart registration and any rental permit will pass to the new owner.

faqs.q: Does my golf cart registration change when I sell the house?
faqs.a: If the cart goes with the house, yes. The seller reports the sale or removes the decals within 10 days, and the buyer registers within 10 days. The city's Ownership Release and Cart Release forms apply, and new registrations are completed at City Hall.

faqs.q: How many short-term rental permits does Peachtree City allow?
faqs.a: The ordinance caps them at 135. Operators with documented rentals before November 7, 2024 had priority, and permits renew every 730 days. Ask the city whether a permit can follow a property to a new owner.

faqs.q: Has the 2026 Peachtree City appeal window closed?
faqs.a: Yes. Fayette's 2026 residential and commercial appeal deadline was July 7, 2026, and each later notice opens a fresh 45-day window. Call the Assessors' Office at 770-305-5376 with questions.

faqs.q: Can a buyer still claim homestead after April 1?
faqs.a: Fayette accepts applications through the end of that year's appeal window, provided the owner lived in the home on January 1. A recent purchase needs a recorded warranty deed or settlement statement and a Georgia driver's license.

faqs.q: Who pays the Georgia transfer tax on a Peachtree City sale?
faqs.a: The seller is liable by statute, and many contracts assign it to the buyer. The Department of Revenue says it is paid before the deed is recorded.
